assets.initial_prompt:
Use case: compositing
Asset type: original 2D character-and-weapon combat grip proof for concept preflight
Input images: Image 1 is the accepted Nyra Kestrel four-view turnaround and is the sole identity/costume reference. Image 2 is the accepted Stormglass Odachi orthographic sheet and is the sole weapon-design reference.
Primary request: Create one polished full-body three-quarter studio view of the exact same adult woman warrior from Image 1, wearing the exact same complete costume, in a grounded ready-to-strike stance while holding the exact same odachi from Image 2 with a physically correct two-handed combat grip. This is a contact and design-consistency proof, not an action illustration.
Subject identity invariants: preserve Image 1’s exact mature face, restrained anime-realism proportions, realistic skin, dark indigo braided high tail, clean hairline, face-framing strands, stature, armor silhouette, matte forged steel plate topology, charcoal leather straps, deep blue-gray woven underlayers, braided cord lacing, small weathered stormglass inserts, protected hips/thighs/knees, articulated gauntlets and grounded boots. Keep full coverage and the same material wear. Do not simplify into civilian clothing or redesign any armor.
Weapon invariants: preserve Image 2’s exact blade silhouette, length, subtle curvature, single sharpened edge, forged steel construction, narrow translucent mineral spine inset, substantial guard, long charcoal leather-wrapped two-hand hilt, structural pins and pommel. Do not redesign, shorten, thicken, duplicate, crop or glow the weapon.
Pose/contact: full body, head through both boots visible, three-quarter view, stable low ready-to-strike stance with weight over both grounded feet and believable balance. The long blade travels diagonally through clear negative space and the complete tip, blade, guard, hilt and pommel are fully inside frame and legible. BOTH hands are in front/three-quarter orientation so both palms and all ten articulated fingers are visibly readable. Each hand physically closes around a different section of the same leather-wrapped hilt, with realistic finger overlap, thumb opposition, knuckle bend, pressure and contact shadows. Hands separated enough for leverage; no gap between skin/gauntlet and grip. Guard remains immediately above the leading hand; trailing hand remains immediately above the pommel. Wrists align naturally with forearms. No body/armor/blade intersections, no floating contact, no fused fingers, no extra digits, no missing digits. No sheath on body.
Scene/background: uniform neutral 18% gray studio background, empty and seamless, one ground baseline, soft flat-neutral presentation lighting, restrained floor contact shadows only.
Style/medium: premium current-generation original anime-realism concept art with realistic materials and anatomy, crisp production rendering, no 3D/game-readiness claim.
Composition/framing: landscape, complete full-body figure centered with sufficient room for the complete diagonal blade; no perspective distortion, no extreme foreshortening, no camera crop, no target or environment, no VFX.
Quality: high; prioritize exact input fidelity, face/costume/weapon identity, complete anatomy and indisputable two-hand contact.
Constraints: one character, one weapon, one blade; all hair, fingers, boots, sword tip and pommel visible; fully covered functional combat costume; no text, labels, letters, numbers, logos, watermark, runes, symbols, decorative border, callouts, target, scenery or glow.
Avoid: civilian jacket or pants, bare thighs, cleavage, fetish styling, pin-up pose, plastic or chrome surfaces, neon, energy blade, floating slabs/tubes, copied franchise motifs, guns, axes, chainsaws, duplicate weapon, impossible grip, hands near rather than around hilt, palm hidden by blade, fused fingers, malformed hands, extra fingers, missing fingers, blade-body intersection, cropped blade, action VFX, dramatic environment.

revisions.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: targeted revision of original 2D combat grip proof
Input images: Image 1 is the rejected first combat-grip composition whose character identity, costume, full-body framing, grounded stance, background, one complete weapon and material rendering must be preserved. Image 2 is the accepted Nyra Kestrel turnaround and remains authoritative for face, hair, body and costume. Image 3 is the accepted Stormglass Odachi sheet and remains authoritative for the weapon.
Primary request: Revise only the forearm/wrist/hand presentation and the nearby weapon orientation enough to make BOTH two-handed grips physically auditable from the palm side. Preserve the successful full-body three-quarter grounded ready stance, exact adult woman identity, exact armor, exact one weapon, complete blade framing and neutral gray studio presentation.
Targeted correction: shift the camera-relative hilt angle and forearm rotation so both hands are viewed from a clear three-quarter palm-side angle rather than a dorsal/knuckle-side angle. For EACH hand, visibly show the palm heel/thenar area, thumb web, opposed thumb, and four separate articulated fingers curling in a complete closed loop around its own separated section of the same leather-wrapped long hilt. Ten digits total, anatomically correct. Leading hand directly behind the guard; trailing hand directly ahead of the pommel. Real pressure compression and contact shadows. Both wrists neutral and aligned to forearms. No gap, no floating contact, no hand-blade intersection, no fused fingers, no extra or missing digits. A slight low diagonal guard position is acceptable if it makes both palm-side grips visible while retaining a credible ready-to-strike posture.
Invariants: exact mature face, dark indigo braided high tail, restrained anime-realism proportions and complete fully covered layered armor from Image 2; exact matte forged steel blade silhouette, mineral spine inset, guard, long wrapped hilt and pommel from Image 3; one character, one weapon; complete head, hair, boots, blade tip and pommel inside frame; protected hips/thighs/knees; grounded feet; neutral 18% gray background; flat-neutral lighting; no sheath.
Quality: high; prioritize palm-side contact evidence and all ten fingers without sacrificing identity or weapon design.
Constraints: no text, labels, letters, numbers, logos, watermark, runes, VFX, target, scenery or dramatic effects.
Avoid: dorsal-only hand view, hidden thumbs, missing fingers, extra fingers, fused fingers, open or hovering grip, fingers resting beside handle, duplicated weapon, altered blade, altered costume, cropped tip, cropped boots, action blur, impossible wrists, intersecting geometry, civilian clothing, cleavage, bare thighs, fetish styling, chrome, plastic, neon.

inspection.notes: Complete character and complete one-blade weapon are legible. Both grounded boots contact the floor; two separated hands close around the same long hilt with visible thumb-web/finger articulation and contact shadows; no visible floating contact or intersections. Minor residual limitation: a mechanically closed grip necessarily occludes the center of each palm, so palm evidence is three-quarter thenar/thumb-web visibility rather than flat open-palm visibility.

rejected_iterations.reason: Rejected despite strong identity, framing, blade legibility and two-hand contact because both grips were shown predominantly from the dorsal/knuckle side; the stricter brief required more auditable palm-side/thenar and thumb-web visibility.
